desnz_ghg_factors.name: UK DESNZ/Defra GHG conversion factors
desnz_ghg_factors.attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
desnz_ghg_factors.note: THE substitute for GLEC/ISO default factors. Freight tonne-km factors by mode and vehicle class, WTT and TTW separated, refrigerant GWPs. OGL v3.0 expressly permits commercial exploitation AND sub-licensing, which is the rare combination we need.

eurostat.name: Eurostat
eurostat.note: Modifications must be flagged to the end user, and a transformation must not imply Eurostat endorsement.

ec_weekly_oil_bulletin.name: European Commission Weekly Oil Bulletin (DG ENER)
ec_weekly_oil_bulletin.attribution: Source: European Commission, Weekly Oil Bulletin (DG Energy). © European Union — reused under Decision 2011/833/EU (CC BY 4.0); changes indicated.
ec_weekly_oil_bulletin.note: Weekly national fuel prices with and without taxes, submitted by Member States and published by the Commission as XLSX. VERIFIED 2026-08-30 against two primary sources, not by analogy to the sibling Eurostat/EUR-Lex entries: (1) the bulletin page itself carries NO dataset-specific copyright notice, so it does not fall in the Commission legal notice's 'individual copyright notice' carve-out; (2) the Commission legal notice states Commission-owned content is licensed CC BY 4.0 under Decision 2011/833/EU, reuse allowed 'provided appropriate credit is given and changes are indicated' — hence the changes-indicated clause in the attribution above, which matters here because we derive numeric series from the published spreadsheets. UNCONFIRMED and recorded rather than assumed away: whether any individual Member State submission carries separate upstream rights. No such notice appears on the publication, and the Commission publishes it as its own document, so the default applies; if a Member State notice ever surfaces, this entry drops to `conditional` and the gate closes automatically.

eia.name: US Energy Information Administration
eia.note: Attribution requested, not compelled. The EIA logo IS a trademark: do not use it.

bls.name: US Bureau of Labor Statistics
bls.attribution: Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics
bls.note: Covers OEWS occupation wages, QCEW county wages, ECEC benefit loading.

ember.name: Ember
ember.attribution: Source: Ember, licensed under CC BY 4.0
ember.note: Grid carbon intensity, the IEA substitute. AMBER SUB-QUESTION: Ember compiles from upstream sources including EIA, Eurostat and the Energy Institute. Its CC-BY covers ITS compilation; confirm no ingested series is an IEA pass-through.

neso_carbon_intensity.name: National Energy System Operator (NESO), Carbon Intensity API
neso_carbon_intensity.attribution: Source: National Energy System Operator (NESO), Carbon Intensity API, CC BY 4.0
neso_carbon_intensity.note: GB grid carbon intensity (gCO2/kWh), keyless JSON API. Licence text as read by the PROD-SRC fact lane on 2026-10-08 (register section 1.5, row D): the API page states "CC BY 4.0", with an "API Terms of Use" pointer on the project GitHub. The Terms of Use were not read by that lane or by lane S8-E5; re-verify if they add a restriction. The producer is scripts/producers/regional/neso-carbon-intensity-producer.mjs; the data_sources row came from migration 378.

eea.name: European Environment Agency
eea.attribution: Source: European Environment Agency (EEA), licensed under CC BY 4.0
eea.note: Explicitly includes commercial purposes. Must not distort the original meaning. Third-party content inside EEA products is carved out and must be checked per dataset.

eurlex.name: EUR-Lex / Official Journal
eurlex.attribution: © European Union, https://eur-lex.europa.eu — reused under Decision 2011/833/EU. Only the Official Journal of the European Union is authentic.
eurlex.note: The authenticity caveat is not optional: we must never imply our copy is the authentic text. UNVERIFIED: the EUR-Lex-specific notice wording (page returned navigation only); the notice above is built from the Commission legal notice plus the standard OJ authenticity clause.

gleif_lei.name: GLEIF LEI
gleif_lei.note: No attribution required. Must not imply GLEIF endorsement. The clean legal-entity key, and the reason organisation identity keys on LEI rather than on a licensed carrier code.

pvgis.name: PVGIS (JRC)
pvgis.attribution: Source: PVGIS, European Commission Joint Research Centre
pvgis.note: JRC states PVGIS output is unrestricted. If we embed raw irradiance rather than PVGIS-COMPUTED PV output, the upstream CM SAF / ERA5 terms apply instead and must be checked.

worldbank.name: World Bank datasets (excl. CPPI)
worldbank.note: The acknowledgment obligation must FLOW DOWN to our customers in our own terms if they can re-use the data. CPPI is a separate, amber entry.

epa_egrid.name: US EPA eGRID and GHG Emission Factors Hub
epa_egrid.note: US grid subregion factors and US-specific emission factors. Pairs with DESNZ for global coverage.

nga_wpi.name: NGA World Port Index
nga_wpi.attribution: Source: US National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, World Port Index
nga_wpi.note: The UN/LOCODE substitute for PORTS, with coordinates and facility attributes.

geonames.name: GeoNames
geonames.attribution: Source: GeoNames, licensed under CC BY 4.0
geonames.note: General place gazetteer, the other half of the UN/LOCODE substitute. Terms read 2026-10-19 with the honest identity CarosLedge/1.0 on https://www.geonames.org/export/ (cc-by licence, credit GeoNames with a link or another reference, commercial use allowed, as is) and the licence line of https://www.geonames.org/about.html (Creative Commons Attribution 4.0). Serves the port place names of src/core/entities/data/unlocode-names.json (R2e M6); the credit travels with attributionsFor.

wikidata.name: Wikidata
wikidata.note: Carries UN/LOCODE values as statements under CC0. Useful as an ALIAS RESOLVER: we resolve a customer-supplied LOCODE to our own node key without publishing the LOCODE list ourselves. Terms re-read 2026-10-19 with the honest identity CarosLedge/1.0: all structured data (main, Property, Lexeme and EntitySchema namespaces) is released into the public domain under Creative Commons Zero. Serves the ISO 3166-1 country names of src/core/entities/data/unlocode-names.json (R2e M6), read from the query service; no credit is required.

emsa_thetis_mrv.name: EMSA THETIS-MRV
emsa_thetis_mrv.licence: EMSA site notice: reproduction authorised provided the source is acknowledged
emsa_thetis_mrv.attribution: Source: EMSA THETIS-MRV. Reproduced with acknowledgement of source.
emsa_thetis_mrv.note: DISCHARGED 2026-08-30 from conditional to permitted. Operator ruling: the EMSA material is free to all, citing https://www.emsa.europa.eu/thetis-mrv.html. Verified the same day against the primary notice at the url above, which states verbatim: "Reproduction is authorised, provided the source is acknowledged, save where otherwise stated." That is an authorisation, not a condition to discharge: this register defines `conditional` as permitted-subject-to-an-act-we-must-perform (notify, register, accredit), and acknowledgement is not such an act — every `permitted` entry here already carries an attribution string (GeoNames under CC BY 4.0 is the precedent). No commercial carve-out and no prior-permission requirement appears in the general case. TWO THINGS RECORDED HONESTLY RATHER THAN GLOSSED: (1) the notice is site-wide, not dataset-specific, and carries a `save where otherwise stated` tail — the THETIS-MRV page itself was read on 2026-08-30 and states nothing to the contrary (it carries no licence wording at all), so the site notice governs; if EMSA ever marks the dataset separately, this entry must be re-verified. (2) EMSA is an EU agency, so Commission Decision 2011/833/EU does not apply to it directly — the authorisation above stands on EMSA's own notice, not on the Commission reuse decision. The prior entry asked exactly that question and it is now moot. Supporting context, not load-bearing: publication is a legal obligation under Regulation (EU) 2015/757 Art. 21, and the annual fleet report is produced by DG CLIMA (European Commission), which would fall under 2011/833/EU in its own right. WHAT THIS UNLOCKS: `verified_operator_avg` (factor-tier rank 2) was structurally empty while this sat amber; it is now seedable. THETIS-MRV is also the substitute for Clean Cargo carrier factors and the lawful source of IMO numbers, so discharging it clears two red entries. Seeding it is separate work and is NOT authorised by this entry alone.

worldbank_cppi.name: World Bank Container Port Performance Index
worldbank_cppi.licence: CC BY 3.0 IGO with third-party carve-out
worldbank_cppi.attribution: The World Bank, Container Port Performance Index. License: CC BY 3.0 IGO.
worldbank_cppi.askWho: World Bank Transport Global Practice (CPPI team), pubrights@worldbank.org
worldbank_cppi.askWhat: Does CC BY 3.0 IGO extend to the CPPI index scores and rankings TABLE, or only the narrative?
worldbank_cppi.note: CPPI is co-produced with S&P Global Market Intelligence and the rights notice puts the burden of clearing third-party components on the reuser. Interim position: cite rankings sparingly with full attribution; do NOT ship the table as a queryable dataset.

clean_cargo_aggregate.name: Clean Cargo aggregate trade-lane averages (public report)
clean_cargo_aggregate.attribution: Smart Freight Centre is acknowledged as the source.
clean_cargo_aggregate.askWhat: Does the report's written-notification clause operate as a standing licence for a SaaS product, or will SFC require a commercial agreement? Also: is the clause still present in the current edition?
clean_cargo_aggregate.note: The 2023 report permits resale/commercial use PROVIDED written notification is given in advance, i.e. notice rather than consent. Notice must actually be SENT and recorded before this moves to permitted. Note the SFC-internal inconsistency: GLEC requires permission, this requires only notification, and the stricter clause governs the GLEC tables.

glec_framework.name: GLEC Framework default emission factor tables
glec_framework.blocker: "No use of this publication may be made for resale or for any other commercial purpose whatsoever, without prior permission in writing from Smart Freight Centre." Free to download is not free to reuse.
glec_framework.note: CRITICAL DISTINCTION, and the thing that saves the build: the METHOD is not protected, the TABLES and TEXT are. We can be GLEC-conformant in method while populating it from OGL and public-domain factors. SFC accreditation may be the legitimate route to the tables, but accreditation is UNVERIFIED as conveying a data licence and must not be assumed to.

iso_14083.name: EN ISO 14083:2023 default values and tables
iso_14083.blocker: The strictest terms in the set. A single NAMED end-user licence that cannot be shared even within our own legal entity, and "integration, embedding, encoding, structuring, transformation, or operationalization of the ISO Publication within any digital or software-based environment" requires SEPARATE licensing. Structured extraction and text/data mining are also barred.
iso_14083.note: Buy ONE copy for a named engineer to read. Implement the calculation logic, which is not copyrightable. Never ship its tables or text.

clean_cargo_carrier.name: Clean Cargo carrier-specific trade-lane factors
clean_cargo_carrier.blocker: Carrier-specific factors are "only accessible to members". No public licence. Whether a member may re-serve them to its own customers is UNVERIFIED, and membership cost is unpublished.
clean_cargo_carrier.note: The Tier 2 slot in the factor hierarchy is DESIGNED for this and stays EMPTY until a membership with redistribution rights exists. The schema is pre-wired; the data is not seeded.

iea_datasets.name: IEA datasets (end-use prices, grid factors, data annexes)
iea_datasets.licence: IEA Terms of Use for Non-CC Material
iea_datasets.blocker: Explicit and describes our exact use case: prohibits disseminating in entirety free or for a fee, prohibits databases "substantially derived from" the material or that "could constitute a substitute", and caps downloadable raw data at five data points.
iea_datasets.note: NUANCE WORTH KEEPING: IEA NARRATIVE content (reports, articles, standalone graphs) IS CC BY 4.0. The prohibition is specifically on datasets, data explorers, data annexes, the Oil Market Report and the Policies and Measures databases. We may cite IEA prose; we may not seed IEA data.

un_locode.name: UN/LOCODE
un_locode.licence: UN Terms and Conditions of Use
un_locode.blocker: "personal, non-commercial use, without any right to resell or redistribute them", and compiling or creating derivative works is prohibited. No open licence exists anywhere.
un_locode.note: THE SURPRISE. LOCODE was assumed safe and is not. Counter-arguments exist (a code list is thin factual data, arguably uncopyrightable; it is embedded in every logistics platform; no known enforcement) but they are arguments for counsel, not a licence. WORKABLE POSTURE: treat LOCODE as an INPUT ALIAS we resolve against, never a dataset we publish. Our node keys are our own, populated from NGA WPI + GeoNames + Wikidata. A customer-supplied LOCODE resolves to our key. Cheap next step: ask UNECE in writing for confirmation of commercial reuse.

scac.name: SCAC codes (NMFTA)
scac.blocker: "No part of the SCAC database may be reproduced or utilized in any form or by any means… without written permission from NMFTA", and may not be "made accessible in any form to any outside parties" without a licence.
scac.note: No open substitute exists. DESIGN RULE: SCAC is an OPTIONAL CUSTOMER-SUPPLIED FIELD they populate under their own NMFTA licence, never a column we seed. US road carrier identity keys on FMCSA USDOT/MC numbers (public domain) plus LEI.

iata_codes.name: IATA airline designators and location identifiers
iata_codes.blocker: The clearest prohibition in the set, and it names our use twice: no redistribution "including without limitation, its clients", and "use or integration of the Codes in any commercial product or service… is strictly prohibited".
iata_codes.note: OurAirports and OpenFlights publish IATA codes as factual data but cannot grant rights IATA asserts, so relying on them does not cure the claim, it only obscures the trail. Prefer ICAO codes where possible and airline LEI for identity. If commercially necessary, BUY the subscription — it is a known, budgetable cost, not a legal grey area.

imo_register.name: IMO ship numbers via the S&P Global register
imo_register.blocker: "not permitted to use these Numbers in any commercial database, commercial web-site or commercial data product" without prior written agreement; automated extraction "strictly forbidden".
imo_register.note: ELEGANT FIX: acquire IMO numbers from EMSA THETIS-MRV and EU ETS MRV publications, which publish them as part of a STATUTORILY MANDATED disclosure. The S&P terms bind users of S&P's site; they do not reach identifiers we obtained from the EU's own legal publication. Using an IMO number as a foreign key is a different act from redistributing S&P's register.

sbti_dashboard.name: SBTi Target Dashboard
sbti_dashboard.blocker: "This does not represent a license to repackage or resell any of the data"; express permission required from BOTH SBTi and CDP.
sbti_dashboard.note: Costs nothing to ask, and SBTi may grant it. Until then the diffusion/lead-time engine cannot seed from the dashboard. Do NOT substitute CDP: its terms are at least as restrictive.
